system_overview: This specification models the Yo-Yo leader election algorithm with pruning, parameterized to verify correctness across all connected undirected graphs over a fixed number of nodes. Unlike the basic pruning specification that operates on a single fixed graph, this version nondeterministically selects the graph's edge set during initialization, enabling verification of the algorithm for every possible connected graph topology of the given size.
actors_and_components: The participants are nodes numbered from one to a parameter specifying the total number of nodes. The edge set is drawn from all possible undirected edges (without self-loops) over these nodes, constrained to form a connected graph. Node roles (leader, source, sink, internal) are determined dynamically based on edge orientations, and nodes communicate via directed messages along oriented edges.
state_variables: The system tracks five pieces of state per node: (1) an activation flag, (2) the current phase (downward or upward), (3) the set of incoming neighbors, (4) the set of outgoing neighbors, and (5) a mailbox of pending messages. Messages in the downward phase carry a sender and a value; messages in the upward phase carry a sender, a yes/no reply, and a boolean prune flag.
initial_state: All nodes start active and in the downward phase with empty mailboxes. A subset of all possible edges is chosen nondeterministically, subject to the constraint that the resulting graph is connected. Edges are then oriented from smaller to larger node number, establishing initial incoming and outgoing neighbor sets for each node.
actions: The actions are identical to the pruning variant of the Yo-Yo algorithm. Downward phase: sources broadcast their identity; other nodes forward the minimum received value. Upward phase: nodes send yes/no replies with prune flags. Pruning removes redundant edges and deactivates lone sink nodes. Edge reversal occurs for 'no' responses. The graph is progressively simplified until only one leader remains.
safety_properties: Type correctness ensures all variables remain in expected domains. A neighbor consistency invariant accounts for edges being reversed or pruned. The specification checks that the system reaches deadlock if and only if the termination condition holds (the minimum node is the leader, all others are inactive, and all mailboxes are empty).
liveness_properties: The algorithm eventually terminates with the minimum-identity node as the isolated leader and all other nodes inactive, for every connected graph topology of the given size.
model_bounds: The number of nodes is provided as a single constant parameter. The model-checking configuration sets this to five nodes. Deadlock checking is disabled. The set of all possible edges is computed as all two-element subsets of the node set.
additional_assumptions: The specification assumes the number of nodes is a positive natural number. It relies on an external community module for checking graph connectivity. Weak fairness is assumed on the next-state action. The nondeterministic edge selection in the initial state allows the model checker to explore all connected graph topologies, at the cost of a much larger state space compared to checking a single fixed graph.
